question.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=6{x}_{1}(t)+7{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t)-4{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

*Hint: The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are $\lambda_1=-1$ and $\lambda_2=3.$*
question.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix differential equation $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)$ for the given system:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118344/assets/99512ca0bae468975d098cf0789926fe6e8f4ef608693129fa57a3dba02c870b.svg)

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A.$

- We are given that the eigenvalues are 

$$
\lambda_1=-1
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\lambda_2=3.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For $\lambda_1 =-1,$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118344/assets/459df7b451dfbcef264fdf3a1af40f05526529934bb2617a8f43599ee56d27d4.svg)
So, we get an eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118344/assets/b4b518f6ec5abed1cefa88d9de3b42ec18a2553426667def4d7eb4a9964a7e56.svg)

- For $\lambda_2 =3,$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118344/assets/2555ccf5ffe3735fc7cbcd5c5cdbab58b5bf63921ede47ee10ba1192a629b6ba.svg)
So, we get an eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118344/assets/26da2e9864ffdb4795701703b58edbee58f73b131cddc7b229b1dc2e007b1678.svg)

Thus, the general solution to the given system is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$
